jess: quick sanity check — bringing up quantized 7B reranker on canonical dev and seeing a small but consistent -0.02 NDCG@10 vs float baseline on the 5k set. anyone seen tiny formatting/tokenization shifts cause this? :thinking:

omar: can you paste the eval summary and the exact command you ran? also which tokenizer/model combo?

jess: pasted output from eval-bot below. eval run used seed=42, truncation=512, doc concat order=title+body. command: ```./eval_rerank --model quant7b-int8 --dev dev5k.jsonl --tokenizer tiktoken --trunc 512 --seed 42```

eval-bot: run complete — metrics: NDCG@10: 0.642 (float baseline 0.662), MRR@10: 0.531 (baseline 0.544), samples=5000, ci_bootstrap(1000)=±0.006

inge: small drop but outside immediate CI? bootstrapped CI overlaps a bit but looks consistent. two quick suspects: 1) query padding/trunc order changed with quant runtime, 2) subtle tokenization mismatch (we recently flipped token normalization on tokeniser config).

lina: +1 on tokenizer mismatch. can you diff the tokenization stats? e.g., average query len tokens, doc len distribution, number of queries hitting truncation.

jess: quick stats — avg query tokens float=34, quant=34; queries hitting truncation float=27, quant=29. weirdly more trunc hits on quant run. I'll dump per-query lengths.

omar: could be that the quant runtime pads to a different max or drops special tokens. also check doc ordering — are you using title-first in both runs? that can affect ranking when relevant signal is in title.

jess: both runs used title+body but I realized eval harness padded with `pad_to_multiple_of=8` in quant pipeline, not in float. that changes batching but shouldn't change tokenization. still, it could change attention masking?

inge: attention masking differences can change scores once quantized; we've seen small calibration shifts from int8 kernels. Suggest running two ablations: (A) exact same tokenization pipeline (serialize/deserialize tokens) then run quant; (B) float model with same batching/pad settings as quant. if drop persists only in quant, it's kernel-level.

lina: also run a paired bootstrap significance test and rank-lift per-query. ping me the per-query deltas; we can look for a small slice where drop concentrates (e.g., short queries, code queries).

jess: plan: 1) re-run tokenization parity (serialize tokens) 2) run float with pad_to_multiple_of=8 3) run paired bootstrap (10000 iters) and produce top-200 worst queries. I'll post outputs here.

ome: sg, thanks. if you want I can spin a quick job that forces identical token bytes between runs to rule out tokenizer drift.

jess: thanks — kicking off jobs now. ETA ~30m. leaving notes for anyone jumping in: pay attention to truncation counts and title/body order; if we see a slice, maybe try small FP16 or per-channel scale tweak to int8 kernel. :thumbsup:

eval-bot: job queued (id=Q-3391). will post results to thread when finished.
